note: Scenarios written from the titles and purposes of the STANDATA variance PDFs, not from matcher output. expected: the variance number(s) a person would say covers or is closest to it; hint: covered_candidate (current 2023 edition) | near_miss (only an earlier edition exists) | none.

scenarios.description: We want to use window opening control devices that comply with ASTM F2090 on the bedroom windows of our apartment building.
We want clear glass in a fire-resistant wall between a corridor and the suites, protected by sprinklers instead of wired glass.
The dryer and bathroom exhaust outlets in our house with a secondary suite are closer than 1800 mm to an air intake under the soffit.
We are installing hydronic radiant heating in a slab on grade and want less than 100 mm of insulation under the heated floor.
We want to build an unvented roof assembly with spray foam insulation on a house.
Protection of vented soffits close to the property line for a house exposure issue.
A multi-level storage racking system with access levels in an industrial warehouse.
A greenhouse covered with polyethylene film.
A permanent wood foundation with mechanical ventilation in a house.
Welding procedures for a structure authenticated by a professional engineer.
An oil and gas processing building that we want classified as a medium hazard Group F Division 2 occupancy.
A mechanical refrigeration system designed to CSA B52:23.
We want to build the walls of a house from structural insulated panels (SIPs).
Residential tall walls higher than 3.6 m using generic engineered details from a guideline instead of project engineering.
Adhered masonry veneer using generic engineering details on a house.
A lowered workspace pit in a service garage.
A six storey apartment building with a single exit stair and four units per floor.
Electric vehicle charging stations in an underground parkade.
Solar panels installed over a green roof on a flat roof of a school.
A hot tub on a rooftop deck of a condominium.
